questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Production Across Countries' refers to.
questions.a: Production of goods and services is no longer confined to a single country. Companies set up plants and offices in different nations to take advantage of lower costs, skilled labour, and access to raw materials, leading to a globally distributed production system.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Production Across Countries'.
questions.a: Production is spread across countries so that each stage of making a product can be done where it is cheapest and most efficient.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Production Across Countries' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Production Across Countries

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Interlinking Production Across Countries' refers to.
questions.a: Production across countries is interlinked through multinational corporations that invest in foreign countries, buy local companies, or place orders for supplies, thereby connecting distant markets and producers into one global network.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Interlinking Production Across Countries'.
questions.a: MNCs interlink production by foreign direct investment (FDI), acquisitions, and outsourcing, tying producers and markets across nations together.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Interlinking Production Across Countries' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Interlinking Production Across Countries

concepts.title: Foreign Trade and Integration of Markets

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Foreign Trade and Integration of Markets' refers to.
questions.a: Foreign trade connects markets of different countries. Producers in one country can sell goods in another, and consumers can choose from goods produced anywhere, leading to integration of markets across borders.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Foreign Trade and Integration of Markets'.
questions.a: Foreign trade creates a wider market where goods, prices, and producers of different countries compete and integrate.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Foreign Trade and Integration of Markets' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Foreign Trade and Integration of Markets

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'What is Globalisation' refers to.
questions.a: Globalisation is the process of rapid integration or interconnection between countries through foreign trade, foreign investment, and movement of people, capital, technology and services across borders.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'What is Globalisation'.
questions.a: Globalisation integrates countries through trade, investment, technology and movement of people, reducing barriers between national economies.

questions.q: Under which section is 'What is Globalisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: What is Globalisation?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Role of MNCs in Globalisation' refers to.
questions.a: Multinational Corporations (MNCs) are companies that own or control production in more than one nation. They play a major role in globalisation by investing capital, transferring technology, and linking production and markets across countries.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Role of MNCs in Globalisation'.
questions.a: MNCs drive globalisation by spreading production, investing across borders, and connecting distant markets through their networks.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Role of MNCs in Globalisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Role of MNCs

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Role of WTO in Globalisation' refers to.
questions.a: The World Trade Organisation (WTO) is an international organisation that sets rules for global trade and aims to liberalise trade by removing barriers, allowing goods and services to flow freely between countries.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Role of WTO in Globalisation'.
questions.a: The WTO promotes free trade by persuading member countries to reduce trade barriers, though its rules are often seen as favouring developed nations.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Role of WTO in Globalisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: World Trade Organisation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Impact of Globalisation on India' refers to.
questions.a: Globalisation has affected India by increasing the variety and quality of goods available, creating new jobs in services and exports, while also threatening small producers and creating insecure working conditions for many workers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Impact of Globalisation on India'.
questions.a: Globalisation has benefited consumers and some industries in India but has hurt small producers and created job insecurity for workers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Impact of Globalisation on India' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Impact of Globalisation in India

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Advantages and Disadvantages of Globalisation' refers to.
questions.a: Globalisation offers advantages like access to wider markets, better technology, more jobs and greater choice, but also brings disadvantages such as inequality, threat to small producers, and job insecurity.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Advantages and Disadvantages of Globalisation'.
questions.a: Globalisation has both positive effects (growth, choice, technology) and negative effects (inequality, loss of small producers, insecurity).

questions.q: Under which section is 'Advantages and Disadvantages of Globalisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Advantages and Disadvantages of Globalisation

questions.q: Using the method 'Liberalisation and Privatisation', work with: foreign_investment = 40, liberalisation = 75, privatisation = 240. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of globalisation.
questions.a: 355 units

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Liberalisation and Privatisation' and work with: foreign_investment = 360, liberalisation = 240, privatisation = 300. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of globalisation.
questions.a: 900 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Liberalisation and Privatisation' refers to.
questions.a: Liberalisation is the removal of government restrictions on the private sector, such as licences and quotas, allowing businesses to operate freely. Privatisation is the transfer of ownership or control of government-owned enterprises to private hands.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Liberalisation and Privatisation'.
questions.a: Liberalisation removes barriers to private business while privatisation shifts ownership from government to private sector; together they opened the Indian economy to globalisation.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Liberalisation and Privatisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Liberalisation and Privatisation
